payload.name: Resolve pronoun antecedents before extracting claims
payload.description: When a statement uses 'they/them' or other pronouns to refer to a previously mentioned entity, use this before extracting a memory to attribute the predicate to the correct subject rather than the speaker.
content: Before extracting a memory candidate, resolve every pronoun in the source message to its nearest plausible antecedent in the same or preceding messages; do not default to the speaker.
When the speaker describes other entities (pets, family, friends) and then uses 'they/them', attribute the predicate to that entity, not the speaker.
If the antecedent is ambiguous or unverifiable, do not guess; either omit the claim or mark it for review instead of assigning a wrong subject.

solves: The extraction stage misattributed the pronoun 'They' in 'They definitely prefer nice, sunny days in the grass' to the speaker instead of her dogs, producing an incorrect memory. The abstract mechanism is failing to resolve anaphoric pronouns to their antecedents before assigning a memory subject. This rule applies to any future construction pass where a speaker mentions entities (pets, people, objects) and later refers to them with pronouns, ensuring claims are stored under the true referent.
